questions.prompt: Which of these countries shares a border with Somalia?

hints.nudge: Two countries are neighbours when you can walk from one into the other. Picture Somalia on the globe and look at what it touches.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Somalia article.

questions.proof: It is bordered by Djibouti to the northwest, Kenya to the southwest, with Yemen to the north, the Guardafui Channel and Somali Sea to the east, and Ethiopia to the west.

hints.nudge: A continent is one of the great land masses of the world. Find Somalia on the Atlas and see which land mass it sits on.
hints.whereToLook: Find Somalia on the Atlas and see which land mass it sits on.

questions.prompt: Which of these countries covers the most ground?

hints.nudge: Area is how much ground a country covers, not how many people live there. A small crowded country can still be small.
hints.whereToLook: Compare the four on the Atlas. Area means how much ground a country covers.

questions.proof: By area: Somalia about 637,657 square kilometres; Uganda about 241,038 square kilometres; Malawi about 118,484 square kilometres; Seychelles about 459 square kilometres.

questions.prompt: Which country has the capital city Mogadishu?

hints.nudge: Every country has one capital city. Find the city in the question on a map, then see which country it sits in.
hints.whereToLook: Look on the Atlas: find the city, then see which country it sits in.

questions.proof: The capital city of Somalia is Mogadishu.

questions.prompt: What is the capital city of Somalia?

hints.nudge: A capital city is where a country’s government meets. The other three are capital cities too, of other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the “Daraawiish State” part of the Somalia article.

questions.proof: This became Italian Somalia in 1905, with capital Mogadishu.
